title: Evaluate prefix, suffix and grammar evidence without script leakage
summary: Reuse existing opening/closing lexical features and test whether syntax, repairs, hedges and phrase structure add useful context beyond scripts and topics. All grammar features are proposed research with explicit parser/ASR uncertainty, not existing identity capabilities.
out_of_scope: Rebuilding existing behavior n-grams under a second service
Using self-introductions or roster names in an acoustics-only result
Treating lexical similarity as calibrated identity probability
implementation: Wrap the existing lexical-timing-v1 output in the experimental feature manifest; retain original definitions and avoid changing B-arm semantics.

Define a bounded grammar candidate inventory with units and source spans: clause/repair/hedge structures, question formation and formulaic openings/closings; select any parser only after dependency/license/reproducibility review.
Tag shared institutional scripts and explicit names/quoted speech through separate field views, with source quality and parser version; unavailable/ambiguous grammar stays unknown.
Compare original lexical support, masked/formula-controlled variants and added grammar over identical queries/reference groups; include topic-swapped and script-shared controls.
Preserve exact evidence shown to a semantic evaluator and outcome qualification per question family; export descriptive features only to the experimental decision layer.

acceptance.criterion: Existing prefix/suffix features retain their original version/meaning and are not counted as a new implemented grammar capability.
acceptance.verification: Compare wrapper output to existing behavior test fixtures and inspect version fields.

acceptance.criterion: Shared scripts and self-introduction names cannot leak into a claimed acoustic-only or name-masked condition.
acceptance.verification: Run sentinel/script controls and verify packet bytes plus separate labeling of explicit-name evidence conditions.

acceptance.criterion: Missing or low-quality ASR/parser output is reported rather than converted into confident grammar features.
acceptance.verification: Use truncated turns, uncertain tokens and malformed parser responses; inspect availability/failure reasons.

acceptance.criterion: Any claimed grammar gain is measured against lexical-only and script/topic controls on the same cohort.
acceptance.verification: Publish paired per-meeting results and errors with frozen feature/config digests.

tests: Two people reading the same formal thanks/motion script
One person speaking on unseen agenda topics
Very short turn with no reliable clause structure
risks: Grammar may mostly measure ASR/editor artifacts rather than a stable speaker characteristic.
Script and role effects can masquerade as personal patterns.

reuse.application: Reuse existing opening/closing n-grams, filler counts and input normalization.
Retain source-score and timing limitations; grammar is an explicitly new research family.

sources: User clarification, 2026-10-08, active Matter build: DIAT owns meeting learning; roughly 315 hours/5–10 recurring people is user-reported; crawler owns jurisdiction knowledge; private exported-data experiments only.
